automations.title: Workflow status pill adds a leading glyph the design's row chip omits

automations.title: Android Message Preview lacks the Error state and template-id entry path iOS has — but the inline-draft path (the only one Android exposes) never errors on either platform
automations.evidence: MessagePreviewViewModel.kt:100-108 defines MessagePreviewUiState with only Loading and Loaded — no Error; start() (55-84) maps NetworkResult.Failure to a Loaded local-interpolation fallback so a failure never surfaces. iOS adds a .error(String) phase (MessagePreviewViewModel.swift:21) and a .template(id:) Source (lines 23-26, 87-92), rendered via AutoErrorView (MessagePreviewView.swift:66-68) and routed (SchedulingRoute.swift:134, SchedulingRouter.swift:208, MessagePreviewStubView.swift:43). Critically, iOS .draft mode also catches preview errors and falls back to local interpolation (fillVariables lines 107-110) — it only reaches .error in the .template(id:) GET path. So for the inline-draft preview both platforms render a fallback and never show an error.
automations.recommendation: Either accept the deliberate local-interpolation fallback for the draft path (it is consistent with iOS draft behaviour), or, if routed template-id preview is wanted on Android, add the template-id entry path plus an Error+retry state to mirror iOS. Otherwise document the asymmetry.
automations.verifierNote: Facts are accurate but the severity overstates impact. The Error state on iOS is unreachable from the inline-draft entry (which is the only path Android has) — both platforms fall back to local interpolation there. The missing piece is solely the secondary routed template-id entry, a non-critical mock surface. The auditor's own recommendation says 'then this is fine.' Downgraded major -> minor.

automations.verifierNote: Verified on both platforms: gated is computed/stored at initial load (iOS isGated flag, Android Error.gated) but the error branch in each view ignores it and shows the generic full-screen error. automations.title: Full-screen editors have no imePadding — the soft keyboard can overlap the message body and the sticky footer while typing

MainActivity.kt:71 calls enableEdgeToEdge() and there is no windowSoftInputMode/adjustResize in AndroidManifest.xml, so the IME floats over content. iOS SwiftUI lifts content above the keyboard by default. Note: imePadding is used nowhere in the entire Android app (0 occurrences), so this is an app-wide convention rather than a defect specific to these screens.

Real friction for the multi-line body editor. Downgraded major -> minor because (a) it is a systemic app-wide convention affecting every text-entry screen equally, not an I16-specific defect, and (b) the body scrolls and the footer remains reachable once the keyboard is dismissed, so content is not blocked.

screens.name: B4 Availability Schedule List
divergences: Empty-state CTA: iOS 'Add working hours' seeds a 9-5 Mon-Fri DEFAULT schedule with rules (createDefaultSchedule, isDefault:true + setRules). Android same CTA calls addSchedule() which creates an empty 'New schedule' with NO rules and opens the editor — different resulting data and different label/intent than design's 'Add working hours'.

Overflow menu surface: iOS uses a native confirmationDialog (action sheet) with Set-as-default/Rename/Duplicate/Delete/Cancel. Android uses an anchored DropdownMenu with leading lucide icons (calendar-check/pencil/copy/trash-2) matching the design's OverflowMenu more closely. iOS drops the per-item icons the design shows.

Delete-default handling: Android intercepts CANNOT_DELETE_DEFAULT and shows a dedicated ReassignDefaultDialog ('Pick a new default') to reassign-then-delete. iOS just surfaces an error alert ('Make another schedule your default before deleting this one') with no reassign flow.

Subline timezone separator: iOS conditionally omits the ' · TZ' segment when timezone is empty (and bolds TZ in fg2). Android always renders '${summary} · ${timezone}', producing a trailing ' · ' with an empty/Auto-detected tz, and renders the whole subline in one fg3 color (no bold-TZ emphasis).
Duplicate copy name: iOS appends ' (copy)' e.g. 'Working hours (copy)'; Android appends ' copy' e.g. 'Working hours copy' (no parens).
Android duplicate also clones date overrides; iOS duplicate clones only weekly rules.
Toast vs alert: Android shows transient bottom ToastPill for action errors; iOS shows a modal 'Heads up' alert.

screens.name: B5 Weekly Hours Editor
divergences: Booking-limits link target diverges: iOS 'Booking limits & notice rules' row calls openBookingLimits() which pushes .eventTypeList(owner:.personal) (a SERVICES LIST), never the B7 sheet. Android navigates directly to BOOKING_LIMITS (the B7 screen, auto-selecting the first event type). Same row, two different destinations.

Timezone 'lock/auto' model: iOS derives lockTimezone = (timezoneId == device) and renders a muted ' · auto' suffix when locked. Android hardcodes lockTimezone=false on load, never derives it, and its timezone field button shows only the city with NO ' · auto' suffix.

Copy-to-days affordance: iOS uses an inline anchored .popover (DayCopyPopover, 192pt) matching the design's floating CopyMenu. Android uses a full ModalBottomSheet (CopyToDaysSheet). iOS pre-checks Mon-Fri (minus source) by default per design; Android starts with NOTHING checked.
Copy-button disabled label: design/iOS show 'Copy to N days' and the iOS/Android button disables at 0. Android's label reads 'Copy' when 0 selected; iOS reads 'Copy to 0 days'.
Time editing: iOS taps a range button to open a wheel DatePicker sheet (start+end). Android opens a ModalBottomSheet with two scrolling 15-min option lists; quantizes to quarter-hours only.

Save chrome: iOS uses FormShell with a sticky bottom 'Save schedule' bar AND hides the nav bar when ready (toolbar hidden). Android uses the custom AvailabilityTopBar (back chevron + centered title, no trailing action) plus a bottom A3SaveBar. Design title 'Set hours' (empty) / 'Edit schedule' — both honor this.
Save dirty-gating: iOS Save is enabled only when formValid && isDirty. Android A3SaveBar is always enabled (no dirty/valid gate on the save button).

screens.name: B6 Date Overrides & Holidays
screens.designId: date-overrides-frames.jsx (Empty/Overrides/Editing/Holidays) — bottom SHEET over dimmed editor
divergences: Presentation: iOS is a bottom SHEET (grabber + 'Date overrides' title + 'Done' button that dismisses) matching the design. Android is a FULL-SCREEN with AvailabilityTopBar (back chevron + 'Date overrides' title + 'Done' text action). Sheet-vs-fullscreen mismatch.

Persistence model: iOS persists immediately on every add/remove/holiday-toggle (persist() calls setOverrides each time). Android batches all edits in local state and only writes them on the top-bar 'Done' tap (save()). On iOS 'Done' just dismisses; on Android 'Done' is the save action. Different data semantics and different unsaved-changes risk.

Header overline: iOS renders 'Personal · Working hours' in the personal sky accent (matches design's E.personal overline). Android renders 'Personal · Working hours' via SectionOverline in personal accent too, but as a scrolling list item, not a fixed sheet header.

Range entry: iOS opens an in-screen child sheet ('Block a date range' with From/Until graphical DatePickers and 'Block these dates'). Android opens two sequential Material A3DatePickerDialog dialogs (start then end) with no labeled composer. Design shows a 'Block a date range' chevron link row only (both add the picker bespoke).
Holiday name divergence (data/copy): iOS USHolidays names the October holiday 'Indigenous Peoples' Day'; Android usPublicHolidays names it 'Columbus Day'. Both build 11 holidays.
Custom-hours editor: iOS uses inline hour/minute DatePickers in the composer card; Android opens the shared TimeRangeEditorSheet (two scrolling lists, title 'Custom hours').
Today marker: iOS calendar tints today's date number in primary600; Android calendar has no today indicator (only selected fill + override dot).

screens.name: B7 Booking Limits & Notice Rules
screens.designId: booking-limits-frames.jsx (Defaults/Custom/Error) — bottom SHEET over dimmed editor
divergences: Reachability: iOS B7 is only reachable as a route taking a specific eventTypeId (bookingLimits(owner:eventTypeId:)) — but the WeeklyHours 'Booking limits' link does NOT open it (pushes eventTypeList instead), so in the Availability flow iOS never lands on this sheet. Android's WeeklyHours 'Booking limits' link navigates straight to this screen.

Event-type selection: Android loads ALL personal event types, defaults to the first, and renders an 'Applies to' selector ('EventTypeSelector' dropdown) when there is >1. iOS receives a single eventTypeId and shows NO selector. Different model entirely.
Empty state: Android has a dedicated Empty state ('No event types yet' / 'Create an event type first…'). iOS has loading/ready/error only (no empty state — it assumes a valid eventTypeId).

Presentation: iOS uses FormShell with a left .close and a trailing 'Done' that dismisses on success (sheet idiom matching design). Android is full-screen with AvailabilityTopBar back chevron + 'Done' text action.

Save model: iOS does PER-FIELD-DIRTY save (only changed fields PUT; caps only sent once moved off the loaded value). Android always PUTs all fields, sending dailyCap/perBookerCap only when > 0 (takeIf{it>0}).
'Max per day' / 'Per-person' zero handling: Android renders 0 as 'No limit' and lets the stepper reach 0 (min 0). iOS clamps these to min 1 and never shows 'No limit'.
'Max per week' placeholder: iOS renders value '–' disabled at 0.4 opacity; Android renders the literal default '20' disabled. Both intentionally omit the backend field but display it differently.
Per-person unit: iOS shows 'booking'/'bookings' (singular at 1); Android shows null unit for <=1 and 'bookings' otherwise (no singular 'booking').

screens.name: B9 Block Off Time
screens.designId: block-time-frames.jsx (Default/Recurring/AllDay/Conflict/Saving) — bottom SHEET over dimmed editor
divergences: Conflict detection: Android actively fetches same-day bookings on every date/time change (checkConflict → getBookings → overlap test), builds the ConflictCard, and wires 'View booking' to navigate to scheduling/bookings/{id}. iOS leaves conflict ALWAYS nil and viewConflictingBooking() is an explicit no-op — the design's conflict frame can never appear on iOS.

Save validation: iOS disables Save when end <= start (isValid gate). Android's top-bar 'Save' is hardcoded enabled=true regardless of whether start<end, so an invalid/zero-length window can be submitted.

Presentation: iOS uses FormShell with .close + trailing 'Save', plus a bottom lock footnote / 'Saving…' shimmer bar (sheet idiom). Android is full-screen with AvailabilityTopBar (back chevron + 'Save'/'Saving' text action) and the lock footnote inline; no bottom saving bar.

Recurrence caption copy: design says 'Repeats every Friday · Ends never. Tap to add an end date.' iOS uses 'Repeats every week · Ends never. Tap to add an end date.' (generic, not weekday-specific). Android uses 'Repeats every Friday. Tap to change.' (weekday-specific but drops the 'Ends never' clause). Three-way copy mismatch.

Reason field helper: iOS shows the helper as a caption below a plain TextField. Android uses an OutlinedTextField with placeholder 'Dentist' and supportingText 'Optional · only you can see this.' (Material chrome vs bespoke).
Block-overlap chip casing: design label 'Booking overlap' (icon + sentence case). iOS renders 'Booking overlap' sentence case; Android renders 'BOOKING OVERLAP' all-caps.

screens.name: B1 Event Types / Service List
divergences: Top bar height: iOS list uses a bespoke 46pt bar (EventTypeListView.topBar, frame height 46 — matches design's 46). Android routes through EtTopBar which is TOP_BAR_HEIGHT = 56.dp (EventTypeKit.kt:81). 10dp taller than design and than iOS.

Permission-gated/read-only state: design FrameGated shows a read-only list + lock banner 'Only owners can edit this catalog.' + disabled toggles + disabled +. Android carries canEdit (disables toggles/menu/+ in Content) but on the Secret error it falls into a full-screen Error state, never the read-only list-with-banner. iOS has NO canEdit/gated concept at all — toggles/menu/+ are always enabled and there is no lock banner.

Delete confirmation: iOS shows an .alert('Delete event type?') BEFORE deleting and surfaces the HAS_UPCOMING_BOOKINGS conflict as an actionError alert suggesting hiding. Android deletes immediately on menu tap with NO pre-confirmation, and only shows a 'deactivate instead' AlertDialog if the server returns 409. Different destructive-action UX.

Overflow menu toggle item: iOS shows a dynamic 4th item ('Hide' with eyeOff when active, 'Make active' with eye when hidden — EventTypeListView.swift:569). Android hardcodes 'Hide' with EyeOff for every row (EventTypeListScreen.kt:417), so a hidden row's menu still says 'Hide'.

'Nothing hidden' empty subcopy differs: iOS 'Hidden event types stay off your booking page. Hide one from its menu.' vs Android 'Event types you hide will show up here.' Also iOS uses .eye glyph for this state, Android uses EyeOff.
Copied-toast check glyph color: iOS uses appTextInverse (white check), Android uses success (green check, EventTypeListScreen.kt:656).

Android exposes a Home (green) pillar variant in PillarIdentityPill/identityIcon; design only draws Personal (sky) and Business (violet). iOS theme also supports Home — both go beyond design, but consistently.

screens.name: B2 Event Type / Service Editor
divergences: Segmented controls: Android uses the design's custom sunken-track EtSegmented for Duration/Location/Assignment/Currency/Collect (matches the JSX Segmented exactly). iOS uses the native SwiftUI Picker(.segmented) for all of these — a completely different visual control (system gray segmented bar, not the design's white-on-sunken pill segments).

Basics text inputs: Android renders bordered EtTextField boxes (1.5px border, radius 8) matching design TextInput. iOS renders bare inline TextFields separated by hairline Dividers inside the card (EventTypeEditorView.basicsGroup) — no bordered input boxes, so the Basics card looks structurally different from the design and from Android.

Assignment segment labels/options: design FrameCollective AssignmentCard = ['Anyone','Specific','Collective'] (3 options). Android matches via ASSIGNMENT_OPTIONS ('Anyone'/'Specific'/'Collective'). iOS renders EventAssignmentMode.allCases = 'One-on-one'/'Round robin'/'Collective'/'Group' (4 options, different labels).

Collective mode: iOS renders a WORKING 'Required hosts' LabeledStepper + a member-avatar stack of user-icon discs (CollectiveMemberAvatarStack). Android renders a DISABLED placeholder EtStepper showing '—' plus a 3-disc initials avatar stack. Functional divergence (iOS editable, Android read-only placeholder).

Stripe-not-connected card color: iOS StripeConnectCard fills the card with businessBg (pillar violet tint) and the icon tile with Theme.Color.business — pillar colors. Android + design use Stripe brand colors (stripeBg #f5f4ff card, stripe #635bff tile). iOS does not use the Stripe brand palette.

'Anyone'/round-robin caption copy: design + Android = 'Any seated teammate who's free can take the booking.' iOS uses EventAssignmentMode.caption = 'Bookings rotate across the team.' for round robin (different copy).

Section gating on create: iOS hides Availability, Advanced, Visibility/Controls and the link-out 'More' card until the type is saved (isEditing) — matching design FrameCreate which shows only Basics/Duration/Location. Android always renders Advanced, Controls and Links (and Availability) even on create.
Location segment order: design + Android lead with 'In person, Phone, Video, Custom'. iOS locationOptions order is 'Video, Phone, In person, Custom'.

Identity pill: iOS editor pill prints Title in .caption (12pt) and NOT uppercased (EventTypeEditorView.identityPill, Text(theme.title)). Design HeaderPill + Android EtIdentityPill are 10pt bold UPPERCASE.
Per-day cap empty value: iOS shows 'No limit' for 0 (and caption '0 means no daily limit.'); Android shows 'Off' with no caption.

Top-bar 'Save' text action: design event-editor-shell TopBar has a 'Save' text action in the bar AND a sticky SaveBar. Both platforms suppress the top-bar Save (iOS via stickyBottom, Android via bottomActionLabel) and show only the bottom bar — shared omission of the top Save affordance.

Save/duration-error toast: Android editor renders the transient toast with an AlertCircle warning glyph (warning tint); iOS surfaces save failures via an .alert('Couldn't save') dialog instead of a toast.

screens.name: B3 Intake Questions Editor
divergences: Reorder interaction: iOS reorders via a long-press Menu with 'Move up'/'Move down' on the grip handle (SwiftUI can't single-handle drag outside a List). Android reorders via a real vertical-drag gesture on the grip (detectVerticalDragGestures). Same visual grip, different mechanics.

Both platforms render this as a routed full-screen FormShell, while the design is a bottom SHEET (24px top-radius, grabber, 'Done', dimmed editor behind). Shared platform deviation — neither shows the sheet/grabber/scrim.
Both port the design's drag-reorder 'lifted'/placeholder frames as best-effort; the design FrameReorder lifted-card and dashed placeholder slot are not reproduced exactly on either platform.

screens.name: B8 Connected Calendars
divergences: Provider tile glyph color: Android tints each provider glyph with its brand color (Google blue, Apple black, Outlook blue — brandColor() from SchedulingPalette, matching design PROVIDERS.color). iOS tints ALL provider tiles with appTextSecondary (grey) — the brand colors are lost.

Helper line placement: design shows the 'Connect a calendar to check for conflicts…' helper in FrameNone/FrameConnecting (not in coming-soon). iOS renders the helper ONLY when isComingSoon and never in the none/connected states (ConnectedCalendarsView.helper). Android shows it in both the empty (coming-soon) and connected lists.
Top bar chrome: Android uses the custom EtTopBar (chevron-left + centered 'Connected calendars' title, 56dp). iOS relies on the system navigation bar (.navigationTitle) instead of a bespoke bar.
Coming-soon hero glyph: iOS uses .calendarSync (matches design lucide calendar-sync). Android uses CalendarCog for the hero AND the toast glyph (wrong glyph).
'Open Settings' icon: iOS uses .settings (gear, matches design lucide 'settings'). Android uses SlidersHorizontal.

Both render B8 full-screen rather than as the design's bottom sheet over the dimmed scheduling hub (shared deviation).

screens.name: A1 Scheduling Hub
divergences: Android renders an EXTRA analytics SummaryCard (This month / Bookings / vs last month / Upcoming / No-shows / sparkline / 'See insights') at the top of the loaded body (HubLoadedBody SummaryCard, SchedulingHubScreen.kt:249) that is NOT in the design frame and NOT on iOS. iOS's hero card is the BookingLinkCard only. Identity pill Business glyph differs: iOS uses .store (matches design lucide 'store', SetupKit.swift:142); Android uses PantopusIcon.Briefcase (SchedulingHubScreen.kt:205).

Loading skeleton: iOS hand-rolls the designed geometry (252 link-card shimmer + 60 pause + agenda rows + 4-row manage group, SchedulingHubScreen.swift:316). Android uses the generic SchedulingLoadingSkeleton(rows=4) — 4 identical white cards each with two shimmer lines (HubStates.kt:215) — which does not mirror the hub's loaded layout or the design skeleton.

Empty-state dashed placeholder icons differ: iOS uses .layoutGrid/.clock/.calendarClock (HubComponents.swift:625); Android uses Grid3x3/Clock/CalendarCog (HubStates.kt:146). Design uses layout-grid/clock/calendar-sync.

Manage-row icons differ: 'Connected calendars' — iOS .calendarSync (matches design calendar-sync), Android PantopusIcon.CalendarCog; 'Settings' — iOS .settings, Android PantopusIcon.SlidersHorizontal; 'Event types' — iOS .layoutGrid (design layout-grid), Android Grid3x3.

Android non-editor top bar shows an Info glyph trailing (SchedulingHubScreen.kt:177); iOS intentionally shows NO trailing control for a non-editor (SchedulingHubScreen.swift:33). Design's permission-gated frame DOES show an info glyph, so Android matches design here and iOS omits it.
iOS Hub footer is translucent (ultraThinMaterial) matching design's backdrop-blur; Android footer is opaque appSurface (HubComponents.kt:658) with no blur.

screens.name: A2 First-run Setup Wizard
divergences: Both implement the same 4-step wizard (Link/Type/Hours/Share) with StepRail, handle field (idle/checking/available/taken+suggestions), type picker, timezone chip, weekly-hours grid, success hero, and resume banner — strong parity.

Disabled primary CTA styling: iOS via WizardShell paints the design's grey 'sunken' fill + muted text; Android WizardShell paints the tinted button at alpha 0.5 (WizardShell.kt:329). Minor visual divergence, both platforms consistent across all wizards.

Android weekly-hours grid order is Sun→Sat (DAY_LABELS, WizardSteps.kt:51) while iOS orders Mon→Sun (WizardHoursGrid weekdays, WizardStepViews.swift:389). Design lists Monday first. iOS matches design ordering; Android leads with Sunday.

screens.name: A3 Scheduling Settings root
divergences: Business 'Team & seats' sub-copy differs: Android uses '4 members · 2 booking seats' (matches design); iOS uses 'Manage members & booking seats' (SchedulingSettingsScreen.swift:168).

Error state retry affordance: iOS renders the design's icon+capsule 'Try again' button (SchedulingSettingsScreen.swift:513); Android uses a plain TextButton('Try again') with no icon/border (SchedulingSettingsRootScreen.kt:239).

Loading skeleton: iOS hand-rolls overline+140-card x3 mirroring the settings groups (SettingsSkeleton, SchedulingSettingsScreen.swift:479); Android uses generic SchedulingLoadingSkeleton(rows=5) (SchedulingSettingsRootScreen.kt:55).
Both render the 'Saving'/'Saved' row states, danger zone, mono footer, segmented New-bookings control, tz-lock affordance — otherwise tight parity.

screens.name: A4 Notification Preferences
divergences: SMS 'coming soon' tooltip: iOS has a tappable S-column header that toggles an 'SMS coming soon' tooltip (smsHint, SchedulingNotificationPrefsScreen.swift:73,450); Android NotifCategoryCard has no smsHint state/tooltip at all (NotifComponents.kt:104). Design includes the 'SMS coming soon' tooltip frame.
Both share the same channel-triad matrix, P/E/S chip states, reminder lead-time chips, legend, pause banner, push-off notice — otherwise strong parity.
Loading skeleton: iOS hand-rolls overline + 220-card x2 (NotifSkeleton); Android uses generic SchedulingLoadingSkeleton(rows=5).

screens.name: A6 Scheduling Onboarding (home+business)
divergences: Both implement Home (3-step: Members/Combine/Share) and Business (4-step: Link/Service/Team/Confirm) with member multi-select, collective/round-robin mode tiles + assignment rule, service tile picker + duration/price, team seating with role chips + seat counter, auto-confirm/approve segmented + explainer, composed-availability card, and pillar success hero — strong parity.

Member/teammate avatars: design uses gradient-filled discs with the member's own initials; both iOS (avatarTone fills) and Android (appSurfaceSunken/appTextStrong fill) render flat tone-tinted avatars — a shared simplification, consistent across both platforms.

Duration control on Business 'Service' step: iOS renders a dropdown Menu '30 min ▾' (matches design Field with chevron-down); Android renders four inline 15/30/45/60 chips (DurationStepperChips, OnboardingSteps.kt:602). Different control shape but consistent intent.

screens.name: D1 Invitee Intake Form
divergences: Architecture: iOS is a standalone pushed route/View (InviteeIntakeFormView + InviteeIntakeFormViewModel) reached via .inviteeIntakeForm; Android is a local step (ConfirmStep.Details) inside the single InviteeConfirmFlow destination (IntakeFormBody). Both render equivalent content but lifecycle/back behavior differs.

Phone field: Android ALWAYS renders a hardcoded required 'Phone number' field in the 'A few questions' section (IntakeFormScreen.kt:186), bound to values.phone. iOS only renders phone when the host schema contains a phone-type question (questionsSection gated on !viewModel.questions.isEmpty, InviteeIntakeFormView.swift:286). On the live public payload (which carries no questions today) iOS shows NO 'A few questions' section at all, while Android still shows the phone field. The two screens are structurally different in the common case.

iOS hold-expired CTA dismisses the whole intake screen (dismiss(), pops the pushed route); Android calls onClose() which closes the flow destination. Functionally similar but iOS expired tap on 'Pick another time' returns to slot picker by popping, Android returns by onClose.

Loading skeleton geometry differs: iOS shows a 120pt card shimmer + a 200-wide bar + three 44pt rows; Android footer shows a shimmer CTA but the body intake loading state is not distinctly modeled (the flow seeds data up front, so Details has no loading skeleton).
Submitting state: iOS dims the form to 0.85 + shimmer CTA 'Submitting your booking'; Android dims to 0.85 + shimmer CTA with the same label. Match.

iOS validates only name/email + required questions (no guest-email validation); Android ConfirmUtils.validateIntake also validates each guest email and phone digit count (>=7) — Android has stricter intake validation than iOS.

screens.name: D2 Review & Confirm
divergences: Architecture: iOS is a separate pushed route (InviteeReviewConfirmView via .inviteeReviewConfirm, reads draft from InviteeBookingDraftStore); Android is the ConfirmStep.Review local step (ReviewConfirmBody) in InviteeConfirmFlow.

Attendee/guests line: iOS shows '+ <guest emails joined>' (attendeeSecondary, InviteeReviewConfirmViewModel.swift:146); Android shows '+ N guest(s)' (a count, ReviewConfirmScreen.kt:147-152). Different representations of the same data.

ApplyCreditRow: iOS renders the dashed 'Apply package credit or promo code' button (design Frames 1-5) as a placeholder; Android omits the ApplyCreditRow entirely (ReviewConfirmBody has no apply-credit affordance). iOS-only element.
CreditChip: iOS renders the '1 session credit applied' green pill when hasCreditApplied; Android has no credit chip. iOS-only.

Deposit note: iOS renders the DepositNote ('You pay a $X deposit now...') below the totals; Android shows the deposit only as a 'Balance at your visit' row inside the breakdown, no standalone deposit note sentence. iOS closer to design.

Refund link: both render shield-check + summary + accent 'Refund policy'. iOS opens a CancellationPolicySheet; Android's onRefundPolicy is a no-op default ({} passed from InviteeConfirmFlow — ReviewConfirmBody is called without an onRefundPolicy override, so the 'Refund policy' tap does nothing on Android).
Slot-taken (409): iOS shows an inline error banner + SlotTakenSheet with alternatives; Android surfaces the shared ConflictAlternativesSheet. Equivalent recovery, different sheet components.
TopBar title: both 'Review & confirm'. iOS uses navigationTitle; Android ConfirmTopBar centered title. Match.

screens.name: D3 Confirmed
divergences: Architecture: iOS is a separate pushed route (InviteeConfirmedView via .inviteeConfirmed(manageToken), which RE-FETCHES the booking via GET /public/booking/:token); Android is the ConfirmStep.Confirmed local step (ConfirmedBody) that reuses the in-flow ConfirmedData (no re-fetch).

Confirmed hero email copy: design + Android show the literal invitee email in bold (Android sentToEmail = values.email; 'We sent the details to <email>'); iOS hero body uses generic 'We've sent the details to your email.' (InviteeConfirmedViewModel.swift heroBody) — iOS drops the email address the design emphasizes.

Account nudge (NudgeCard): design FrameConfirmedFree includes a 'Create an account to manage your bookings' nudge; Android renders AccountNudge on the free-confirmed frame (ConfirmedScreen.kt:103); iOS does NOT render any account nudge — missing on iOS.
Receipt 'emailed' line: design shows 'Receipt emailed to maya.chen@gmail.com'; iOS shows 'Receipt emailed to you'; Android shows 'Receipt emailed.' — both drop the literal email, with different copy.
iOS renders confetti via ConfettiBurst overlay (suppressed under reduceMotion); Android via ConfettiSpray (suppressed when system animations off). Both gated, match.

Pending-approval: both render info halo + 3-step timeline + ETA pill + dock 'Done'/'Message host'. iOS Message host opens host page URL; Android onMessageHost is a default no-op ({}) wired through ConfirmFooter — Android 'Message host' does nothing.

Add-to-calendar: iOS opens a real AddToCalendarSheet (EventKit/.ics); Android fires an ACTION_INSERT calendar intent directly (no provider-picker sheet, no .ics generation). The add-calendar sheet design (add-calendar-frames.jsx) is implemented on iOS, not on Android.
Dock close/X: both render an X close at top-left and a sticky dock with 'Add to calendar' primary + 'Done' secondary. Match.

screens.name: D4 Manage Booking
divergences: Architecture: both are standalone fetchable destinations (iOS InviteeManageBookingView via .inviteeManageBooking(token); Android ManageBookingScreen at booking/{manageToken}). Aligned.
Status pill: both use shared SchedulingStatusPill with matching labels (Confirmed/Pending/Past/Cancelled). Match.

Window-closed: iOS keeps the disabled action buttons tappable and routes to .inviteePolicyBlocked (I7) on tap; Android disables the action rows entirely (clickable(enabled=false)). iOS has an extra routed policy-blocked path Android lacks.
Book-again: iOS pushes .inviteeLanding(slug); Android navigates SchedulingRoutes.publicBooking(slug). Equivalent.

Contact host: iOS opens https://pantopus.com/book/<slug> via openURL; Android 'Contact host'/'Request a new link' both call onBack/onBookAgain (no host-page URL open) — Android contact-host is weaker.

Cancel sheet: iOS uses a dedicated CancelBookingSheet; Android uses a local CancelSheet with a reason field. Reschedule: iOS InviteeRescheduleView sheet; Android local RescheduleSheet + ConflictAlternativesSheet. Equivalent.

screens.name: C1 Booking Page Management
divergences: Android adds an extra 'Preview your page' LinkRow (eye icon → PUBLIC_PAGE_PREVIEW) in the LinksCard that does NOT exist in iOS and is NOT in the design (design LinksCard has only 'Intake questions' + 'Connect Stripe').
iOS has a dead `previewRequest`/fullScreenCover for the C2 preview but nothing ever assigns it — iOS has NO in-screen path to the public preview; Android does (the extra row).

Android management exposes a NeedsSetup/zero-state branch directly (when no event types & not live) so the H16 zero-state can render inside the management route; iOS management has no zero-state branch (always loads the form because the page is auto-created server-side).
Android 'Intake questions' row shows a value ('Add an event type first' when no event type, else null); iOS shows no value (questionCount = nil). Design shows '2 questions'.
iOS only shows the 'Connect Stripe' payments row when owner.supportsPayments (Personal hides it); Android always shows the Stripe row regardless of owner.
iOS top bar = FormShell with a back chevron + 'Save changes' bottom bar; Android = bespoke BLTopBar + BLSaveBar. Functionally equivalent but separate implementations (parity risk).

iOS optimistically toggles per-service visibility AND status with server round-trips immediately; Android stages all edits (status, services, fields) and only commits them in a batch on Save — different save semantics for the status toggle and service toggles.

screens.name: C3 Share booking link sheet
divergences: iOS QR is a real scannable CoreImage QR (and Save-to-Photos renders a real QR at print resolution); Android renders a deterministic DECORATIVE (non-scannable) QR grid and saves that decorative grid to Photos — the Android 'Scan to book' QR will not actually open the booking page.

iOS 'Show on my profile' / 'Add to email signature' toggles persist via callbacks to the VM (onToggleShowOnProfile→setListed, onToggleSignature); Android's ShareSettingsCard toggles are local-only `remember { mutableStateOf(...) }` — they do nothing and reset every time the sheet reopens.
iOS regenerate confirm uses a native .alert; Android uses a custom Dialog card (matches design's modal better). Both acceptable.
iOS draft-banner 'Turn on' button is conditional on onTurnOnPage being non-nil; Android always shows it.

screens.name: C2 Booking Page Preview
divergences: Paused state: iOS renders the design's NoticeCard exactly (60pt sunken circle + lucide `moon` + 'Your page is paused' / 'Turn it back on in Booking link to take bookings.'). Android routes the paused state through the shared PausedExpiredUnavailableState which uses an 84dp halo + `PauseCircle` icon — wrong icon glyph (design = moon) and a different (app-level terminal) layout.

iOS public-render event-type selected card + ring + 'Pick a time' CTA are fixed brand sky (primary600) per design ('the public render uses brand sky regardless of owner pillar'); Android uses pillar.accent for the selected card border, selected tile bg/icon, ModeChip, AND the Pick-a-time CTA — wrong accent for Home/Business owners.

iOS exposes extra honest states (expired → calendarClock, unavailable/fully-booked → calendarCheck) in PageOffNotice; Android's preview VM only emits Loading/Rendered/Notice/AllHidden/Error (no expired/unavailable distinction in this surface).
Android adds a not-yet-published Notice ('Your page is off' / 'Publish it in Booking link…') for the slug-blank/not-live case; iOS preview VM (not fully shown) maps to pageOff. Copy differs.
Android ModeChip fallback label is 'Online' for unknown modes; iOS LocationChip falls back to 'Video call'. Different default copy.

Android dark preview chrome cannot bleed behind the status bar (Scaffold already insets the route, then PreviewBar adds statusBarsPadding → effectively double padding / no edge-to-edge dark chrome); iOS lets the dark chrome ignore the top safe area.

screens.name: C4 One-off Link Generator
divergences: Android OneOffLinkGeneratorViewModel HARDCODES owner = SchedulingOwner.Personal (no ownerRelay) — pillar chip + owner context are always Personal even for Home/Business; iOS threads the real owner through the VM.

Android 'Offer specific times' generates SYNTHETIC proposed slots locally (buildSlot: tomorrow 9:00am + N days, no availability check); iOS fetches REAL public availability via SchedulingPublicEndpoints.slots and lets the user pick/add from actual open times. Android's proposed times are fabricated.
Android 'Single use' option uses PantopusIcon.Tag; design + iOS use lucide `ticket` (.ticket) — wrong icon glyph.

iOS shows an inline warning card + 'Add a service' CTA when the owner has no event types (configuring with empty options); Android shows a full-screen EmptyState 'Create an event type first' (NeedsEventType). Different empty-state shape.
Android MetaChip shows 'Multi-use' when not single-use; iOS OneOffMetaPill omits the single-use segment entirely when singleUse is false (design only ever shows 'Single use').
Android 'Add a time' just appends a synthetic slot; iOS 'Add a time' opens a Menu of real fetched slots to choose from.
Android ExpiryOption.None encodes 525600 minutes (1 year) for 'No expiry'; iOS .never sends nil expires_in_min (true no-expiry). Data-contract difference.
iOS error frame keeps the Generate button inline below the error note (design Frame 4); Android keeps the bottom GenerateBar + an inline ErrorNote with try-again (both functional but layout differs).

screens.name: H16 Booking Page Zero / Get Started
divergences: There is no dedicated zero-state frame in booking-link-frames.jsx (closest is the 'draft' frame), so both platforms are improvising the H16 hero — neither has a true design reference.

iOS H16 is a standalone routed screen (BookingPageZeroStateView, route .bookingPageZeroState) with two variants (hasEventTypes ? 'Set up your booking link'/link icon : 'Start taking bookings'/calendarPlus) + a secondary CTA; navTitle 'Get started'.

Android does NOT have a standalone H16 route — the zero-state (BookingPageZeroState/EmptyState) is rendered INLINE inside BookingPageManageScreen's NeedsSetup branch, and also reused for event-types/inbox/availability via SchedulingZeroKind.

Copy differs: iOS headline 'Set up your booking link' / sub 'Your services are ready. Claim a link people can use to book you.' / CTA 'Set up booking link'; Android headline 'Set up your booking link' / sub 'Pick a handle and turn on a service, then people can book you with one link.' / CTA 'Set up booking link'.
iOS icon for the has-services hero is .link, no-services is .calendarPlus; Android BookingLink kind always uses PantopusIcon.Link (no two-variant split on whether services exist).

iOS CTA routes to .firstRunWizard(owner:) / .eventTypeEditor; Android NeedsSetup CTA routes to SchedulingRoutes.SETUP_WIZARD only (no add-event-type variant), and the standalone-screen secondary CTA does not exist on Android.

screens.name: C5 Booking Landing / Booker Profile
divergences: GROUP-EVENT FRAMES MISSING ON BOTH: design FrameGroup + FrameGroupFull render a GroupEventCard (seats pill '4 of 8 spots left'/'Fully booked', filled 'Save your spot' CTA, 'Join waitlist' when full). Neither iOS BookingLandingView nor Android LandingLoaded renders any group-event card; both only render the simple EventTypeRow list.

TEAM/COMPOSED FRAME MISSING ON BOTH: design FrameTeam shows a 3-avatar TeamCluster + a ComposedPill ('Times come from each member's availability'/'Round-robin'). iOS HostAvatar and Android HostAvatar only render a single avatar; neither has the cluster or the composed pill.
OPEN-IN-APP CTA: Android wires 'Open' to navigate to OPEN_IN_APP_INTERSTITIAL (BookerLandingScreen.kt:87); iOS 'Open' is an empty no-op (BookingLandingView.swift:150).
PAUSED ICON: design 'moon'. iOS .moon (match); Android PantopusIcon.PauseCircle (BookerLandingContent.kt:318). iOS-vs-Android glyph mismatch.
EMPTY ICON: design 'calendar-off' on rounded-square. iOS .calendarOff rounded (match); Android CalendarX on a circle (BookerLandingContent.kt:333). Wrong glyph + tile shape on Android.

ERROR STATE: design + iOS show a compact link-2-off Notice + Powered-by footer (no banner). Android routes 404 to the shared PausedExpiredUnavailableState terminal screen ('Get the app' dock, different copy). Structurally different error surfaces.
SHARE BUTTON: iOS no-op `Button {}` (BookingLandingView.swift:124); Android fires a real system share intent (BookerLandingContent.kt:169). iOS share does nothing.
RECAP SHEET: Android adds a BookingHandoffSheet after slot selection (BookerLandingScreen.kt:101); iOS pushes straight to intake. Extra Android surface.

BANNER LIGHT STOP (non-personal): Android Home/Business banners use homeBg/businessBg as the light stop (BookerLandingContent.kt:63-64) vs the design's lighter green-300/violet-300; minor tonal divergence.

screens.name: C6 Date + Time Slot Picker (+ C7 Timezone Selector)
divergences: SLOT-SELECT FLOW: iOS selectSlot pushes straight to intake on tap (no Continue bar); Android keeps the slot selected and requires a second tap on a docked ContinueBar. Major flow divergence.
DOCKED CONTINUE BAR EDGE/INSET (Android): ContinueBar at BottomCenter with no nav-bar/IME inset (SlotPickerScreen.kt:205-213) can sit under the gesture bar. iOS has no such bar.

DAY-FULL COPY: iOS + Android both use 'No open times this day'/'Try another highlighted day…'; design says 'No times left this day'/'Every slot on this day is booked.' Both match each other, diverge from design.
NO-AVAILABILITY ICON: design 'calendar-off'; iOS .calendarSearch (renders as bare magnifyingglass); Android CalendarClock. Three-way divergence.
'PICK A DAY' INTERSTITIAL (Android-only): Android adds a selectedDay==null state 'Pick a day with open times' (SlotPickerScreen.kt:494); iOS auto-selects first available day.
SLOT-JUST-TAKEN ROW: design shows strikethrough + 'Just taken' WARN pill on the row + toast. Android strikes through only (no pill); iOS shows no row treatment at all (only the toast).
RESCHEDULE / RESCHEDULE-CUTOFF FRAMES: design frames not implemented inside the picker on either platform (handled by separate reschedule screens). Equal gap.
TZ OVERRIDE 'Reset' ICON: design rotate-ccw; iOS .rotateCcw (match); Android RefreshCw. iOS-vs-Android glyph mismatch.
TZ OVERRIDE BANNER BORDER: iOS primary100; Android infoLight. Minor token mismatch.
TZ SHEET DETENTS: iOS .sheet allows .medium + .large; Android ModalBottomSheet(skipPartiallyExpanded=true). iOS allows a half-sheet the design's tall sheet doesn't.

screens.name: C8 No Availability / Slot States
divergences: DEDICATED ROUTED SCREEN: iOS has a standalone NoAvailabilityView/ViewModel (routed full screen, scans months, hands back to C6). Android has NO routed C8 screen — no-availability is only inline in SlotPickerScreen + the shared terminal FullyBooked state.

FRAME 4 (No-times-anywhere): iOS implements .noAvailabilityAnywhere ('Notify me' primary + 'Join waitlist · N waiting' secondary). Android explicitly defers Frame 4 (SlotPickerScreen.kt:476). iOS-only state.

FRAME 5 MEMBER CLUSTER: iOS drives the composed-empty member cluster from real [SchedulingMemberFreeBusy] (hidden when empty). Android hardcodes AR/JL/MK placeholder members (MemberFreeBusyRow). Android shows fabricated data.
COMPOSED PILL ICON (Frame 2): design calendar-range; iOS .calendarRange (match); Android Calendar (DateRange). iOS-vs-Android glyph mismatch.
FRAME 2/5 ENTRY: neither C6 ViewModel emits composing/composed-empty in the public flow — the states are unreachable dead UI on both.
ROUTED-C8 ACCENT (iOS): NoAvailabilityViewModel hardcodes accent = primary600 (line 39) — the routed C8 CTA is always sky-blue even for Home/Business hosts, unlike the pillar-tinted inline C6 card.
LOADING SKELETON (iOS routed C8): shows only 4 bare slot-row skeletons (no header/calendar), not mirroring the loaded geometry the design keeps. Android C6 loading keeps full chrome.

screens.name: D5 Slot Taken / Conflict Recovery
divergences: Top-bar title differs: iOS uses navigationTitle "Pick a time" (SlotTakenScreenView.swift:27); Android custom top bar literal "Pick a new time" (SlotTakenScreen.kt:123).
iOS uses a SwiftUI nav bar (no custom back chevron drawn); Android draws an explicit ChevronLeft back button in a custom Row top bar (SlotTakenScreen.kt:112-121).

Alternatives subtitle copy diverges: iOS SlotTakenSheet supports a takenTimeLabel ("Someone grabbed 2:00 PM first…") but SlotTakenScreenView never supplies it, so iOS shows the generic fallback; Android hardcodes "Someone grabbed that time first. Here are the closest open times — these are still open." (SlotTakenScreen.kt:145).
Halo size differs: iOS errorBlock halo is 64/50 (SlotTakenSheet.swift:83-87); Android shared EdgeHalo is 66/52 (EdgeComponents.kt:106-108).
Fully-booked body max-width: iOS 208 (SlotTakenSheet.swift:197) vs Android 220dp (SlotTakenScreen.kt:199), and copy "we'll text you" (iOS) vs "we'll let you know" (Android, SlotTakenScreen.kt:195).
iOS adds a standalone .error EmptyState case (SlotTakenScreenView.swift:62); Android has no separate error branch (refreshing/alternatives/fullyBooked only).

screens.name: D6 Payment Failed / Retry
divergences: Presentation model differs fundamentally: design D6 is a bottom SHEET over Review&Confirm. Android implements it as a ModalBottomSheet (PaymentRetryScreen.kt:98) — correct. iOS implements it as a full-screen pushed NavigationStack view with navigationTitle "Payment" and a safeAreaInset dock (PaymentFailedView.swift:21-31) — wrong archetype vs design.

Succeeded copy diverges: iOS "Your second card worked. Taking you to your booking." (PaymentFailedView.swift:134) matches design; Android "Your card worked. You're all set." (PaymentRetryScreen.kt:243) does NOT match design.
Succeeded title diverges: iOS "Payment went through" (design); Android shows "Payment received"/"Payment went through" depending on a processing flag (PaymentRetryScreen.kt:238).
Succeeded CTA: design auto-advances with no button; Android adds a "Done" GhostButton (PaymentRetryScreen.kt:252) not in design; iOS has no button (matches design).

Declined card row: iOS uses a creditCard glyph badge labelled "Your card" (PaymentFailedView.swift:288-301); Android uses an EdgeSavedCardRow with a CardBrand.Generic "CARD" text badge (PaymentRetryScreen.kt:169). Both deliberately avoid a fake masked PAN; design shows a Visa brand badge + "Visa •• 4421".

iOS adds a notApplicable state ("You're all set", PaymentFailedView.swift:192) for paid-off; Android renders a PaidGate fallback Text "Online payments aren't enabled yet." (PaymentRetryScreen.kt:108) — different copy/shape.
HoldChip text on iOS uses a single .timer glyph for both held & released (PaymentFailedView.swift:265); design uses timer vs timer-off. Android also uses Timer for both (PaymentRetryScreen.kt:222).

screens.name: D7 Unavailable / Expired / Terminal
divergences: Dock button ORDER inverted on Android: design + iOS render filled "Get the app" ABOVE ghost "Back to Pantopus" (TerminalStateView.swift:126-127). Android PausedExpiredUnavailableState renders secondaryAction (ghost "Back to Pantopus") ABOVE primaryAction (filled "Get the app") (PausedExpiredUnavailableState.kt:158-159) — self-documented as a shared bug.

dockExtra placement differs: iOS pins the status-specific secondary CTA (Request new link / Notify me) INSIDE the dock above Get-the-app (TerminalStateView.swift:134-151). Android cannot (shared dock only has 2 slots) so it pushes that button UP into the centered body 'extra' slot (UnavailableExpiredScreen.kt:222-227) — structurally different.

iOS exposes 6 statuses (notFound/private/expired/paused/fullyBooked/cancelled) via TerminalKind; Android SchedulingTerminalState adds extra Offline/Blocked/Unavailable states (PausedExpiredUnavailableState.kt:53-61) not in the design's 6.
Private-link body copy: iOS "…or enter your access code below." (TerminalStateView.swift:335) vs Android "…or enter your access code." (PausedExpiredUnavailableState.kt:50).

Android primary CTA uses PantopusTextStyle.body (16sp regular) for the Get-the-app label (PausedExpiredUnavailableState.kt:195); iOS uses 14/bold (TerminalStateView.swift:295) matching the design's 14/700.
Android primary CTA lacks the design's primary shadow; iOS applies pantopusShadow(.primary) (TerminalStateView.swift:303).

screens.name: D9 Open in App Interstitial
divergences: Both platforms implement only the 3 native frames (resolving / resolved / failed); both omit the 2 web frames (smart-banner, stay-on-web) — acceptable on native and consistent.

IdentityLine copy differs: iOS shows "Continuing as <inviteeName> · times in <tz>" from real data (DeepLinkHandoffView.swift:167-172); Android hardcodes the placeholder "Continuing as you · times in local" (OpenInAppInterstitialScreen.kt:264) because the Resolved state carries no invitee profile.
Event preview subtitle: iOS composes duration · price · with-host (DeepLinkHandoffView.swift:138-152); Android renders only state.subtitle if present (OpenInAppInterstitialScreen.kt:215).

Resolved layout: iOS wraps content in a ScrollView with a safeAreaInset dock (DeepLinkHandoffView.swift:84-110); Android centers content in a fixed Column with an absolute-positioned BottomCenter dock (OpenInAppInterstitialScreen.kt:100-113) — no scroll, can clip on small screens.

Brand mark: iOS hand-draws the concentric-ring glyph (DeepLinkHandoffView.swift:229-242); Android substitutes PantopusIcon.Concentric≈RadioButtonChecked (OpenInAppInterstitialScreen.kt:397) — approximation noted in code.
Failed body max-width: iOS 250 (DeepLinkHandoffView.swift:190) vs Android 244dp (OpenInAppInterstitialScreen.kt:337).

screens.name: D10 Policy Blocked / Reschedule-Cancel Cutoff
divergences: iOS is a pushed NavigationStack view with navigationTitle "Your booking" + a system back chevron (PolicyBlockedView.swift:29); Android draws a custom top bar with an explicit ChevronLeft + centered 15sp title (RescheduleCancelPolicyScreen.kt:122-143).

Cancel confirmation UX differs: iOS uses a .confirmationDialog (PolicyBlockedView.swift:32-39); Android opens a full CancelSheet ModalBottomSheet with an optional reason field (RescheduleCancelPolicyScreen.kt:500-550). The reason field is Android-only.

Reschedule UX: Android presents a RescheduleSheet ModalBottomSheet with slot list / conflict / no-slots states (RescheduleCancelPolicyScreen.kt:453-496); iOS calls viewModel.reschedule() to push a route (PolicyBlockedView.swift:178) with no inline sheet.
Android adds a ProposedReschedule policy mode ("Your host proposed a new time", RescheduleCancelPolicyScreen.kt:439-446) with Accept/Decline CTAs that iOS does not have.

Partial-refund note copy: iOS "Cancelling now refunds <X> of the <Y> you paid" (PolicyBlockedView.swift:360) vs Android "Cancelling now, within 24 hours of your visit, refunds <X> of what you paid." (RescheduleCancelPolicyScreen.kt:418).

Policy-card title color: design uses tone-dark (amber-900 WARN_DK). Android EdgeTone.dk maps Warn/Error/Success titles to appText/near-black (EdgeComponents.kt:78-85); iOS EdgeNoteCard title is also appText (EdgeComponents.swift:147) — both approximate, but neither uses the amber-dark shade.
iOS adds a "See full cancellation policy" link opening CancellationPolicySheet (PolicyBlockedView.swift:213-223, 94-100); Android has no equivalent see-full-policy sheet on this screen.

screens.name: D11 My Bookings (customer)

Occurrence conflict copy: iOS "<time> is taken that week" (RecurringSetupView.swift:564); Android "That time is taken" (RecurringSetupScreen.kt:563).

screens.name: E8 Group Roster & Seats
divergences: Top-bar trailing overflow: iOS always shows a 'more-vertical' Menu with 'Message all attendees' + 'Mark no-show'; Android only shows the overflow when loaded.data.canMarkNoShow is true, and its only item is 'Mark no-show' (no 'Message all'). Seated-row status pill + kebab: both render them. Android kebab dropdown shows 'Pending approval' (a no-op disabled-looking item) for non-confirmed rows; iOS kebab just opens the nudge sheet (no per-status menu).
Empty-state disc tint: iOS uses theme.accentBg token; Android uses accent.copy(alpha=0.12) (translucent accent) — slightly different shade than the design's solid identity bg.

Loading skeleton: iOS header shimmer height 118 + 3 row shimmers height 60; Android uses the generic SchedulingLoadingSkeleton(rows=4) which does not mirror the capacity-header geometry the design shimmer shows.
Both implement under-capacity / full / waitlist-active / loading / empty / error. Parity is otherwise close.

screens.name: E12 Manual / On-behalf Booking
divergences: Step 3 Details: iOS renders BOTH design branches — a search field, a verified-invitee accent card (Frame 3), and the unregistered branch with a blue 'Not on Pantopus yet' info banner (Frame 4). Android renders ONLY a plain name input + Invite-by rows; it has NO verified-invitee card, NO 'Not on Pantopus' banner, and NO search-styled field (uses a generic name TextField).

Step 4 Review toggle copy: design + iOS = 'Skip approval / Confirm the booking now' and 'Skip notifications / Don't notify the invitee'. Android = 'Skip approval / Follows the event type's approval setting' (wrong subtitle) and 'Skip notifications' with NO subtitle.
Step 4 toggle component: design + iOS render plain bordered toggle rows with no leading icon. Android uses ExtrasChannelRow with leading BadgeCheck / BellOff icons — extra icons not in the design.
Step rail label typography: iOS active label 11.5/bold; Android uses PantopusTextStyle.small (14) SemiBold — larger/heavier than design's 11.5.
Created confirmation: iOS subtitle personalizes ('We've added it and notified {name}.') matching design 'notified Dana'; Android is static 'We've added it and notified your invitee.'
Created success disc: design = 78pt, iOS = 78pt; Android uses ExtrasIconDisc which is hardcoded 40dp — the success halo is roughly half the design size.

Field placeholders: design/iOS phone='Phone number', note label='Note for the invitee' placeholder='Add a note (optional)'. Android phone='Mobile number', note label='Note (optional)' placeholder='Anything they should know…'.

Both share the StepRail / EventType tiles / day strip + slot list / Review summary card / DoubleBook + SlotTaken conflict surfaces, so the skeleton matches; the divergence is concentrated in Step 3 and the toggle/created details.

screens.name: E13 Waitlist Management (host)
divergences: Scope: iOS WaitlistManagementView targets a single eventTypeId passed in. Android WaitlistScreen is arg-less and resolves the owner itself, then renders an EXTRA 'Event type' picker chip row at the top (data.options.size > 1) — a whole section the design and iOS do not have.

Top-level empty state copy differs: iOS = 'No one's waiting' / 'When this event fills up, people who join the waitlist show up here.' Android top-level Empty (no event types) = 'No waitlists yet' / 'Create a bookable event type to start collecting a waitlist.', and a SECOND entries-empty inside Loaded = 'No one's waiting' / 'When this event fills up, people can join the waitlist and you'll promote them here.' Two different empty copies on Android vs one on iOS.

Capacity stat strip: iOS CapacityHeaderCard is called WITHOUT showStats (single-row capacity bar, no Confirmed/Pending/Waitlisted cells); Android passes showStats=false too — matches. Both omit the stat strip per the design's lean waitlist header.
Section overline copy: iOS = 'N seat(s) open · promote available' / 'All seats filled'; Android = same. Match.
Both implement host promote-enabled / capacity-full(disabled) / loading / error. The structural divergence is the Android event-type picker + the differing empty copy.

screens.name: E13 Waitlist Join (invitee sheet)
divergences: Joined/Already 'in line' position badge: iOS renders a positionBadge helper (currently nil → hidden, but the '#N in line' chip is implemented). Android omits the position badge entirely in both confirmation states.
Joined confirmation copy: iOS = 'We'll text you if a spot frees up.' Android = 'We'll text you the moment a spot frees up.'
Already-waiting subtitle: iOS includes the join date ('You joined this waitlist on {date}. …') when available; Android always shows 'We'll text you the moment a spot opens.' with no join date.

Both render the fully-booked pill, window label, tz chip, name + mobile fields, and a 'Join waitlist' / 'Leave waitlist' CTA. Field fill radius: iOS uses Radii.md (8) matching design; Android uses Radii.lg (12) via ExtrasInputField.

screens.name: E9 Booking Filter / Search
divergences: Presentation architecture: design is a single bottom-sheet over the Bookings list. iOS matches — BookingFilterSheet is a .sheet presented from BookingsInboxView. Android implements a WHOLE separate full-screen BookingSearchFilterScreen (topbar 'Search bookings' + back + filter icon, a LazyColumn results list, its own Loading/Empty/Error) and presents the filter as a nested ModalBottomSheet. The design's filter sheet is one frame; Android added an entire search-results screen around it.
Android filter sheet is a Material3 ModalBottomSheet (default detent/drag handle) vs iOS custom grabber + .presentationDetents([.large]). Android has no explicit grabber row; relies on M3 default.

Android no-results behavior: the count==0 branch in FilterSheetContent returns the NoResultsBlock but STILL renders the sticky 'No matches' disabled CTA. iOS matches that. Both keep search + active summary visible above the no-results note — matches design FrameNoResults.
iOS sheet drives a live recount via task(id: filterSignature) and shows 'Show N bookings' CTA. Android also recounts (draftCount) and labels the CTA via ctaLabel. Functionally parallel.

Owner-context chip accent: design pre-selects the active scope's identity color (business purple in the frame). Both apply pillar tints. Android selected-chip fill is accent.copy(alpha=0.12); iOS uses the real *Bg tokens (personalBg/homeBg/businessBg) — Android's translucent fill is a slightly different shade.

screens.name: E10 Post-meeting Follow-up
divergences: Presentation: design is a bottom sheet over the booking detail (grabber + dimmed parent). iOS matches — BookingFollowUpSheet uses .sheet with ExtrasSheetGrabber + .presentationDetents([.large]). Android renders a FULL-SCREEN Scaffold with a SchedulingTopBar titled 'Follow up' + back chevron — sheet-vs-fullscreen divergence.

Header: design + iOS show an in-body 'Follow up' title + subtitle 'Garden walkthrough · Mara Reyes · Jun 9'. Android ALSO shows 'Follow up' in the top bar AND repeats 'Follow up' as the in-body header — a duplicated title because Android added a top bar the design doesn't have.

Default-state CTA: iOS isSaveNoteOnly = (message empty && outcome nil) → Frame 1 shows the ghost 'Save note only' enabled. Android isSaveNoteOnly = (outcome null && message blank && privateNote NOT blank), and canSubmit requires message/note/outcome — so the blank default shows a DISABLED solid 'Send follow-up', not the design's ghost 'Save note only'. Different default CTA + tone.

Outcome template copy drift between platforms: No-show iOS='…Here's a link to grab another time.' Android='…Here's a link to grab another time whenever works for you.'; Rebook-needed iOS='Let's find another time that works for you — here's my booking link to grab a slot.' Android='Let's find another time that works better — grab a slot here whenever you're ready.'

Sent success scene: both render a dimmed scrim + 72 success disc + 'Follow-up sent' + dark recipient toast. On Android it is drawn over the full-screen content (Box fillMaxSize) with the toast at vertical=Spacing.s8 from bottom; iOS draws it as an overlay inside the sheet.
Rebook chip / push toggle / send CTA accent: both correctly keep these on brand primary600 (not pillar accent) per the design. Outcome chips use the pillar accent on both.

screens.name: E11 Double-book Warning
divergences: Both render soft (calendar-clock amber disc, tappable conflict card, 'Book anyway' primary) and hard (lock error disc, home-tinted member-availability note, disabled 'Can't book — member unavailable', 'Cancel' + 'Pick another member') variants. Close parity.

Scrim/centering: iOS uses a custom ExtrasDialog overlay (appText.opacity(0.5) scrim, maxWidth 300, Radii.xl2). Android uses a system Dialog with widthIn(max=300dp). Both match the design's centered confirm-modal geometry.
Soft-overlap message text color: design uses fg2 (appTextStrong); both use appTextStrong. Match.
Hard-conflict member note: both use HOME palette (homeBg / home dot / homeDark) per the design's green pill, even though the dialog is presented in a business context — correct per spec.
Action CTAs on both platforms correctly use fixed primary600 (not the owner pillar accent), matching the design's hardcoded PRIMARY.

screens.name: E1 Bookings Inbox
divergences: Scope pills: iOS renders all four pills but disables them (.allowsHitTesting(false), BookingsInboxView.swift:137) — the inbox is single-owner per route, so 'All' is never reachable and cross-owner switching is impossible. Android pills are fully interactive (selectScope), re-resolve owners via HomesRepository/AuthRepository, and 'All' unions every owner (BookingsInboxViewModel.kt:97,146).
Member-gated banner (design Frame 9): Android renders MemberBanner ('You're seeing bookings assigned to you', BookingsInboxScreen.kt:679); iOS has no member banner at all.
Auto-confirm hidePending (design Frame 8): Android hides the Pending segment when hidePending is set (BookingsInboxScreen.kt:394); iOS always shows all four tabs.
AssignedChip (design Frames 2/7 — 'Priya'/'Devon'/'Unassigned'): Android renders an AssignedChip on business rows (BookingsInboxScreen.kt:646); the iOS BookingRowView has no assigned-member chip.

Search field placement: iOS shows the search field as a SEPARATE row below the top bar, keeping the 'Bookings' title + search + filter icons (BookingsInboxView.swift:28,203). Android replaces the title + filter icon inline in the top bar with back + field + X (BookingsInboxScreen.kt:219).
Search placeholder copy: iOS 'Search by name' (BookingsInboxView.swift:206) vs Android 'Search invitee name' (BookingsInboxScreen.kt:282).

Inbox quick Decline: iOS opens the E3 decline sheet (presentDecline → .decline sheet, BookingsInboxViewModel.swift:232); Android calls declineBooking directly with no reason sheet (BookingsInboxViewModel.kt:348).
Pull-to-refresh: iOS has .refreshable (BookingsInboxView.swift:289); Android has none (refreshes only on ON_RESUME).
Empty subcopy copy: iOS 'When neighbors book time with you…' vs Android 'When people book time with you…' (BookingsInboxView.swift:399 / BookingsInboxModels.kt:101).

Scope label: iOS pill shows bare 'Business'/'Home'/'Personal' (BookingFilterViewModel.swift:69); Android resolves 'Home · <name>' / 'Business · <name>' (BookingsInboxViewModel.kt:156,166), matching the design's 'Home · Riverside' / 'Business · Acme Studio'.

screens.name: E2 Booking Detail
divergences: Overflow 'Mark no-show' (post-event): iOS adds it to the detail overflow and calls actions.markNoShow directly with no confirmation dialog (BookingDetailViewModel.swift:154,241); the Android detail overflow has no Mark-no-show item at all (DetailTopBar menu only Decline/Reschedule/Reassign/Cancel, BookingDetailScreen.kt:344).

No-show banner glyph: iOS uses .userX (BookingDetailSections.swift:30); Android uses PantopusIcon.UserMinus as a stated substitute (BookingDetailScreen.kt:456).
Rebook/Completed dock icon: iOS uses .rotateCcw for Rebook (BookingDetailView.swift:221,234, design rotate-ccw); Android uses RefreshCw (BookingDetailScreen.kt:1032,1061).
Rescheduled banner: Android adds an extra 'This booking was rescheduled' info banner (BookingDetailScreen.kt:463) that iOS does not render — not a design frame.

Assigned-member card label: both render literal 'Team member' rather than a real name (data gap on both); iOS uses a userRound glyph tile (BookingDetailSections.swift:160), Android uses initials text (BookingDetailScreen.kt:846).

screens.name: E2a Approve / Decline Sheet
divergences: Conflict 'View' link: Android conflict banner link reads 'View' (ApproveDeclineSheet.kt:318); iOS reads 'View conflict' (ApproveDeclineSheet.swift:231) — design says 'View conflict'.

iOS conflict banner is gated by a host-passed showConflictWarning flag (default false, ApproveDeclineSheet.swift:116); Android gates on state.hasConflict — both effectively never show until backend supplies the flag (parity preserved).

screens.name: E2b Reschedule / Reassign Sheet
divergences: Timezone chip: iOS chip is interactive ('Times in <zone> · tap to change' → opens TimezoneSelectorSheet, RescheduleReassignSheet.swift:127); Android TzChip reads only 'Times in $tz' and is NOT tappable (RescheduleReassignSheet.kt:273) — design copy includes '· tap to change'.

Reassign-only mode: Android has a dedicated reassignOnly path titled 'Reassign' with a vertical MemberList (RescheduleReassignSheet.kt:94,426); iOS has no reassign-only title variant — reassign always rides the full reschedule sheet via the avatar rail.
Member rail trailing affordance: iOS adds a '+'/'Keep' chip to keep the current host (RescheduleReassignSheet.swift:354); Android member rail has no keep-current chip.

Conflict recovery: iOS uses SlotTakenSheet (RescheduleReassignSheet.swift:50); Android uses the shared ConflictAlternativesSheet (BookingDetailScreen.kt:241) — both recover a 409, different shared component.

screens.name: E2c Cancel / Refund Sheet
divergences: Non-refundable disabled state (design Frame 4): iOS wires refundNonRefundable (dims section + mutes value) but hardcodes it to false (CancelRefundSheet.swift:75); Android has no non-refundable dim path at all. Both effectively never show it (data gap), iOS is structurally closer.
Retry-refund icon: iOS uses .rotateCw (design rotate-cw, CancelRefundSheet.swift:133); Android uses RefreshCw as a stated substitute (CancelRefundSheet.kt:183).
Restore-credit tile bg: iOS tints the ticket tile with the owner accentBg (CancelRefundSheet.swift:358); Android hardcodes primary50 (CancelRefundSheet.kt:423).

screens.name: E2d Mark No-show
divergences: Reachability: on BOTH platforms the dialog is only presented from GroupRosterScreen, never from the single 1:1 Booking Detail. iOS detail does a direct no-confirmation markNoShow; Android detail has no no-show entry point. So the 1:1 confirmation frame (design Frame 1) is unreachable on both.
1:1 body text color: iOS uses appTextStrong (fg2, MarkNoShowDialog.swift:48); Android uses appTextSecondary (fg3, NoShowSheet.kt:108) — design body is fg2.
Group note field leading icon: Android adds a MessageSquare leading icon in the note (NoShowSheet.kt:127); iOS note field has no leading icon (design note has none).

screens.name: E2e Send Nudge
divergences: Composer placeholder copy: iOS 'Write a message to your attendees…' (SendNudgeSheet.swift:101) vs Android 'Write a quick update for your attendees…' (NudgeSheet.kt:155).
Both are reached only via GroupRoster; the no-recipients disabled state (design Frame 4) is implemented on both (recipientCount==0).

screens.name: F4 Find a Time Setup
divergences: iOS renders a first-class in-sheet COMPUTING state (FindATimeSetupView.computingBody, spinner + 'Checking everyone's availability' + 3 shimmer rows) mirroring design Frame 4; Android FindATimeSetupScreen has NO computing state — submit() validates and immediately navigates, so design Frame 4 (Computing) is unrepresented on Android.

Leading top-bar control: iOS uses FormShell leading: .close (an X, matching the design sheet's cancel/close affordance); Android FtTopBar shows a back CHEVRON (PantopusIcon.ChevronLeft) as the leading control — wrong chrome for a sheet/modal that the design draws with a Close.

iOS presents Setup as a FormShell sheet (matches design Sheet); Android wraps it in a plain Column + FtTopBar full-screen. When reached as F5's Edit it is hosted in a ModalBottomSheet, but the standalone F4 route is full-screen, not a sheet.

Avatar coloring scheme differs: iOS MemberAvatarBadge uses a deterministic per-user gradient (MemberAvatarTone.tone(for:)); Android FtAvatar uses a fixed 6-color flat palette indexed by userId.hashCode() — different per-member colors across platforms.
Explainer overlay-step icon: iOS uses .layers (matches design lucide 'layers'); Android substitutes PantopusIcon.Grid3x3 (icon-set has no layers glyph).
iOS primary explainer line is colored appTextStrong (#374151); Android colors it primary800 (#075985, matching design's '#075985'); iOS is the divergent one here.

screens.name: F5 Suggested Times
divergences: Best-slot computation differs: iOS picks the best slot by MAX free-count (bestSlotStart = suggested.max by freeCount); Android hardcodes isBest = (i == 0) — only the first row ever gets the BEST badge regardless of free-count, so the badge can land on different slots than iOS for the same data.

Booked success copy differs: iOS bookedView headline 'Added to the family calendar' with body '<title> · <label>'; Android Booked headline same but body '<label> is set. Everyone you picked can see it.' and primary CTA 'Done' (iOS uses 'Back to calendar' with .home icon).
Sticky 'Send proposal' footer material: iOS uses .ultraThinMaterial translucent footer (design StickyFooter); Android uses an opaque appSurface Box — both sticky but different treatment.
No-overlap body copy: iOS 'Their free hours don't overlap this week.' (matches design); Android 'Their free hours don't overlap this window.'

No-overlap headline count source: iOS uses members.count; Android parses the first digit out of header.peopleLabel (state.header.peopleLabel.firstOrNull{it.isDigit()}) which is brittle (breaks for 10+ members).

Single-best card: iOS uses an explicit BEST MATCH pill + 19pt day + 15pt time and a wider radius (Radii.xl2 / 20); Android SingleBestCard uses FtChip 'BEST MATCH' + h3 day + body time + Radii.xl (16) — slightly different type scale and corner radius bucket vs design's 18-radius card.

screens.name: F6 Poll Response
divergences: Submitted/success copy differs: iOS submittedView 'Response submitted' / 'We'll let everyone know which times work for you.' / CTA 'Done'; Android PollSubmittedBody 'Response submitted' / 'Thanks for weighing in. The organizer will pick the best time.' / CTA 'Done'.

Organizer header glyph differs: design shows the organizer's avatar photo + 'Mom is finding a time'; iOS uses a generic .users disc; Android uses a .userRound disc. Both drop the organizer NAME (show the poll title instead) — a shared degrade, but the placeholder glyph differs between platforms.
Vote-control track radius: iOS clips the segmented track at Radii.md (8); Android also Radii.md (8) — matches; design is 9. Both round down identically.

iOS hosts the screen with navigationTitle 'Respond' (inline) and relies on the pushed nav back button; Android FtTopBar forces backIcon = PantopusIcon.X (a Close) — design SheetBar uses cancel='Close', so Android's X is closer to the design than iOS's chevron back.

screens.name: F7 Who Is Free
divergences: Explainer-line + hint icons: iOS uses .layers and .handPointer (match design lucide); Android substitutes Grid3x3 and Hand (icon-set gaps) — different glyphs.

Offline banner body copy: iOS 'Showing last synced' / 'Reconnect to refresh availability.'; Android 'You're offline' / 'Showing last known availability. Connect to refresh.' — different title AND body.

Popover behavior: iOS uses a native .popover anchored to the tapped free cell (true cell anchoring); Android uses a Compose Popup anchored to the top of the grid card (not cell-anchored, by its own admission an approximation).

Popover card border color: design popover uses a neutral N.border 1px hairline; iOS popoverCard has NO border; Android TappedActionCard uses a HomeAccent (green) border — neither matches, and they differ from each other.
Empty-state 'Try next week' button: iOS label 'Try next week'; Android label 'Try the next window' — different copy.

Empty banner: iOS hand-rolls an info banner with .calendarX; Android uses FtBanner(tone=Info). Android empty banner body interpolates state.windowLabel ('...booked up for <window>'); iOS body is static 'Everyone's booked up. Try next week...'.
iOS offline gating uses NetworkMonitor.shared.isOnline read inline; Android observes viewModel.isOnline StateFlow — both mute Add when offline, parity preserved.

screens.name: Resource List
divergences: Both render the same 5 frames (empty-templates / loaded / loading / error / offline) with the same bespoke ResourceRow + TEMPLATES quick-start. Top bar = centered 'Resources' title + trailing 'Add' text action + Home-green FAB on both.
Empty-frame subcopy: iOS uses 12pt regular caption, Android uses PantopusTextStyle.caption — equivalent. Both omit design's FAB on loading/error/offline.

iOS 'Add' top-bar action uses Theme.Color.home (home-green); Android ResourceScaffold 'Add' action in Empty/Error uses primary600 (blue) while the Loaded/Loading shell path uses the shell's own color. Minor color inconsistency between the two Android render paths and vs iOS (see finding).
Android error 'Retry' pill = primary600 blue; iOS error 'Retry' = HomePrimaryButton (home-green). Cross-platform divergence on the retry CTA color (see finding).

screens.name: Resource Editor
divergences: Both: name+type / Photo / Who-can-book (segmented) / Booking-rules disclosure / Available-hours / delete. Both render create/edit/invalid/saving/delete-confirm states with the same custom delete dialog.

Available-hours TIME entry differs: iOS uses two inline SwiftUI DatePickers (.hourAndMinute) in the card; Android uses a single 'Available hours' value row (sunken pill) that opens a chained start→end time-picker dialog — matching the design's HoursWindow value row. iOS diverges from design here; Android matches.

Who-can-book 'Specific' member list: design shows mom/dad/ava check rows; both iOS and Android render the 'all members can book / coming soon' caption instead when no roster is loaded — same deferral on both.
iOS booking-rules disclosure default-collapsed in both create and edit; Android defaults expanded when editing (rulesExpanded = !isCreate). Minor cross-platform state difference.

screens.name: Resource Detail
divergences: Both render header rules card + pending-approval badge + approval-queue card + day-sectioned bookings + sticky 'Book this' / 'Book next opening' footer + fully-booked banner. Same loading skeleton, same error frame.
Both use the same approval-queue overline color: iOS Theme.Color.warning, Android PantopusColors.warmAmber (the warning700 token). Effectively matched.
Neither platform renders a distinct offline frame for F11 (design has no offline frame for F11 either) — consistent.

screens.name: Book Resource
divergences: Both: rule reminder chips (neutral) + When section (day stepper + 4-col hour grid + status line) + For-whom picker + Notes + sticky 'Submit booking' + confirmed/approval success screens. States covered identically (default/conflict/violates/submitting/confirmed/approval).

Conflict 409 handling: iOS presents the shared SlotTakenSheet with its DEFAULT title; Android presents ConflictAlternativesSheet with explicit title 'That time was just taken'. Different sheet titles/copy across platforms.
Success halo: iOS uses a RadialGradient halo (matches design radial-gradient); Android uses a flat solid homeBg/warningBg circle. Minor visual divergence.
For-whom control: iOS uses a SwiftUI Menu; Android uses a Material DropdownMenu — both render the avatar+name+chevron row identically. Platform-idiomatic, fine.

screens.name: Schedule a Visit
divergences: MAJOR shared scope reduction vs design: design F13 is an offer-slots engine (VisitExplainer + title/type + who-must-be-home + 'Offered window' date-range value row + 'Visit length' stepper + WEEKDAY GRID + 'Offer these times' preset chips + Access note + 'Generate a shareable booking link' TOGGLE, then states no-host-available / generating / link-created). BOTH iOS and Android instead collect ONE concrete visit (single Date picker + Start-time picker + length) and skip the weekday grid, offer-time chips, shareable-link toggle, and the generating / link-created / no-host states. The divergence is consistent across both platforms (same backend deferral), so iOS↔Android parity holds.

Top-bar commit label differs across platforms: iOS labels it 'Schedule' (rightActionLabel: "Schedule"); Android labels it 'Next' (matches design SheetBar action='Next'). iOS copy diverges from both Android and design.

Both render explainer + title/type chips + who-must-be-home + when(date/time/length) + access note + 'Link an access code' view-only row. Visit-type chips both restricted to Vendor/Guest (design has 4: Vendor/Guest/Delivery/Service).

screens.name: Visit Detail
divergences: MAJOR shared scope reduction vs design: design F14 has 9 states (offered/reserved/confirmed/completed/cancelled/no-show/active-link/expired-link/revoked) plus a Share&Manage card (link status, Copy/QR, Revoke/Extend/Preview, slots reserved/open) and a status timeline that can show terminal states. BOTH iOS and Android collapse to a 2-state lifecycle (confirmed/done), drop the entire Share&Manage / booking-link surface, and drop reserved/cancelled/no-show/link banners. Consistent across both platforms.

Both: teal-gradient avatar (categoryUnboxing tokens) + teal visit-type chip + sunken time row + 4-step status timeline + 'On the home calendar' banner (confirmed) + host card + access card + footer (Cancel/Reschedule or Book-again) + trailing message-circle button. Edit sheet writes via PUT events.

Done-state banner: iOS renders NO banner in done state (EmptyView, matching design Completed which has none); Android renders a 'Visit complete / This visit has passed.' banner in done state (LifecycleBanner Done branch). Cross-platform divergence — Android adds a banner the design and iOS omit.
Removed/cancelled: both show a dedicated 'This visit was cancelled' removed body after a cancel.

screens.name: F1 Home Calendar / Agenda

Android footer Box has no hairline top divider (design/iOS footer has a top border); Android pinned footer uses appSurface with no top rule.
Loading skeleton: iOS hand-rolls a 64/56 shimmer + 3 checkbox rows; Android uses generic SchedulingLoadingSkeleton(rows=4) — different skeleton geometry.

screens.name: H1 Default Reminders Quick-Setup
divergences: Owner/pillar: iOS DefaultRemindersViewModel takes owner via the route (.personal/.home/.business) so the accent + accentBg follow the pillar (sky/green/violet); Android RemindersQuickSetupViewModel hardcodes owner = SchedulingOwner.Personal, so Android always renders the sky pillar and can never show the Home-green / Business-violet check-circle + Push chip the design says 'renders with other pillar accents too'.

divergences: NO design frame exists for the Message Template Editor (no template-editor JSX anywhere in the design dir).

screens.name: H7 Message Preview
divergences: NO design frame exists for Message Preview.

Entry points differ: iOS MessagePreviewView has TWO inits — inline draft AND a routed templateId entry (MessagePreviewViewModel.Source.template(id) loads via GET /message-templates); Android MessagePreviewSheet is sheet-only with a draft (no templateId source, no .messagePreview route exists on Android at all).

Error state: iOS preview VM has a .error(message) phase rendering AutoErrorView with retry; Android MessagePreviewUiState has only Loading/Loaded (no Error case) — the network failure path silently falls back to local interpolation, so Android can never show a preview error.
Loading affordance: iOS shows a ProgressView spinner; Android shows a plain 'Rendering…' Text. Both deviate from the 'never a screen-level spinner' state rule, but differently.
send-test note tone: iOS renders the test note with success OR error tone (testNoteIsError); Android always renders AutoTone.Success. Functionally the same coming-soon copy.
Common: Push/Email/In-app/SMS underline tabs (Push first), per-channel device mocks over a sunken stage, 'Send test to me' ghost, Edit + 'Looks good' footer.

Owner/pillar: iOS carries owner (FAB + empty hero take the pillar accent + theme.ctaShadow); Android TemplateLibraryViewModel hardcodes SchedulingOwner.Personal and AutoFAB has no shadow.

Search field shape: iOS field has a 1px appBorder stroke; Android SearchField has background fill but no border stroke — minor visual difference.
